ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis represents the direction from south to north, and “Qinling” is marked in the middle; on the left side there is a scale for “≥10°C accumulated temperature,” with values of about 1500—7500, and beside it there is also a scale for “annual precipitation (mm)”; on the right side there are scales for “temperature (℃)” and “elevation (m).” Multiple curves are superimposed in the figure, and there are labels such as Jia, Yi, Bing, and “July mean temperature.” Then reason: The question asks to determine the ≥10°C accumulated temperature curve; one should choose the curve whose value range matches 1500—7500 and which, as latitude increases from south to north, has decreasing heat and an overall downward trend. The curve labeled Yi in the figure has higher values on the southern side and generally decreases northward, matching the rule that ≥10°C accumulated temperature decreases from south to north. Therefore, the ≥10°C accumulated temperature curve corresponds to Yi.
